    if df.empty:
        result = {
            'sum': 0,
            'mean': np.nan,
            'min': np.inf,
            'max': -np.inf,
        }
        # Provide a default range to avoid ValueError when plotting empty data
        _, _, plot = plt.hist([], bins=10, range=(0, 1))

            'sum': col.sum(),
            'mean': col.mean(),
            'min': col.min(),
            'max': col.max(),

        if clean_col.empty:
            _, _, plot = plt.hist([], bins=10, range=(0, 1))

            _, _, plot = plt.hist(clean_col, bins=10)

    if df.empty:
        result = {

        }
        # Provide a default range to avoid ValueError when plotting empty data

    else:
        col = df[column]
        result = {
            'sum': col.sum(),
            'mean': col.mean(),
            'min': col.min(),
            'max': col.max(),

        # Drop NaNs to avoid issues with matplotlib hist
